REPORT AT A GLANCE 
 
 
Housing  
33 houses at Blundell Wood, Edenderry 
were completed in early December 2019.  
Houses were allocated, pre-tenancy 
training course held and keys were 
distributed to tenants on 12th December 
2019.  The official opening of the estate 
will be arranged over the coming weeks. 
 
 
Public Participation Network 
On the 4th – 5th December 2019, Green 
Offaly hosted a “Future Farming Forum” 
event in the Bridge House Hotel, 
Tullamore.  The event was well attended 
by members of the farming community in 
Offaly and Guest Speakers explored the 
impacts, challenges and opportunities of 
the changing climate to farming.   
 
 
Built Heritage Investment Scheme & 
Historic Structures Fund 2020 
The Built Heritage Investment Scheme 
seeks to encourage the leveraging of 
private capital to invest in a number of 
small scale, labour intensive projects to 
repair and conserve Protected Structures 
and Proposed Protected Structures and in 
certain cases, for the conservation of 
structures. Closing date for all schemes is 
Friday 31 January. Guidelines and 
Application forms for can be downloaded 
from the Offaly County Council website.

Grand Canal Greenway 
 Works 
are 
continuing on 
the 
Ballycommon to Kilbeggan link of 
the Grand Canal Greenway. This 
relates to a 4km stretch from 
Ballycommon to the Wood of O 
Bridge. This stretch will be complete 
by the end of January.  A decision is 
awaited regarding further ORIS 
funding to allow further works 
towards Kilbeggan. 
 A contractor has been appointed in 
respect of 6kms of the Grand Canal 
Greenway from Digby Bridge to 
Ballycommon Bridge. This section is 
funded under the National and 
Regional 
Greenway 
Fund. 
(Department of Transport Tourism 
and Sport, (DTTAS)) 
 Works on the Grand Canal Greenway 
in the Tullamore Environs from 
Cox’s Bridge, Tullamore to Srah 
Bridge, Ballydrohid (2km) are also 
expected to commence in early 2020. 
This section is funded under the 
URDF for Tullamore. 
 The Part 8 for the extension of the 
Grand Canal Greenway from Turraun 
to Shannon Harbour (16km) is at an 
advanced stage of preparation and is 
expected to be published in February 
2020.

Housing Update 
 33 
houses 
at 
Blundell 
Wood, 
Edenderry were completed in early 
December 2019.  Houses were 
allocated, pre-tenancy training course

Bodies. 
 13 Mortgage to Rent applications 
were finalised in 2019. 
 30 Rebuilding Ireland Home Loans 
applications were received to date; 15 
RIHL have been approved; 8 loans 
paid to date.

Housing Grants 
The Department provided approval in the 
sum of €1,600,000 for 2019 Housing Grants. 
Accordingly, Offaly County Council’s 2019 
contribution towards the grants increased to 
€320,000.   81 Housing Aid for Older Person 
grants, 19 Mobility Aid grants, and 70 
Housing Adaption grants were paid out. A 
new streamlined single Application Form to 
cover the three grants available under the 
Housing Adaptation Grants for Older People 
and People with a Disability Scheme will be 
implemented from 1st February 2020.  
Revised guidance documents for the scheme, 
will also issue. 
 
ROADS 
The Roads Programme 2019 is complete 
throughout the County with all grant claims 
successfully submitted to the TII and 
Departments.  
 
 
Offaly County Council received the 2020 
National Roads Allocation of €3,150,855 
from the TII. The allocation includes funding 
for the N52 Tullamore to Kilbeggan Link 
major scheme and N62 Cloghan to 
Derrinlough minor works scheme. €1.5m has 
been allocated for pavement schemes and 
€500,000 for Road Safety Improvement 
Schemes.   
 
We will be notified of the grant allocation for 
the Regional and Local roads in the County 
in January. The 2020 Roads Programme will 
be prepared for March 2020.

Environment 
A total of 964 complaints in relation to waste 
and litter were investigated in 2019..  Legal 
proceedings were instituted in 9 cases 
resulting in 4 convictions with the remaining 
cases ongoing. A new bottlebank has been 
put in place at Kilclonfert, opposite the 
Community Centre. 
 
Water Quality 
Water Framework Directive – EPA meeting 
with Local Authorities was held on 9th 
January to review the outcomes of the 2019 
programme and roll out the National River 
Water Monitoring Programme for 2020.

LOCAL & COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT 
Local Community Development Committee 
(LCDC) 
The LCDC met on 12th December 2019.  
Agenda items included Rural Development 
LEADER Programme 2014 – 2020 and 
Social Inclusion Community Activation 
Programme (SICAP) 2018 – 2022.  The 
SICAP Annual Plan 2020 was presented to 
the members and agreed and approved in 
principle.  The 2019 SICAP Case Study was 
presented to the members in video format 
and 
demonstrated 
the 
difficulties 
encountered by persons with disabilities and 
members of the wider community from dog 
fouling.  The outcomes of the project showed 
excellent 
collaboration 
between 
the 
community and the agencies involved with a 
commitment by the Council to follow up on 
issues identified.

Age Friendly Strategy 
Creating a great place in which to grow old 
is the aim of the World Health Organisation 
(WHO) inspired movement to cater for an 
ageing population, with Ireland leading 
internationally in rolling out the programme. 
On Monday 16th December 2019, the 
Cathaoirleach of Meath County Council, 
Wayne Harding, welcomed the Taoiseach, 
Leo Varadkar TD and Alana Officer, WHO, 
to Slane Castle to formally recognise the 
response of all 31 Local Authority led Age 
Friendly Programmes with a presentation of 
charters. Bridie Costello- Hynes, Offaly Age 
Friendly Coordinator accepted the charter on 
behalf of Offaly Age Friendly Alliance.  
 
 
Public Participation Network 
On the 4th – 5th December 2019, Green 
Offaly hosted a “Future Farming Forum” 
event in the Bridge House Hotel, Tullamore.  
The event was well attended by members of 
the farming community in Offaly and 
explored the impacts, challenges and 
opportunities of the changing climate to 
farming.  Guest speakers on the day included 
Alastair McKinstry – Climate Scientist at the 
Irish Centre for High End Computing 
(ICHEC) in NUIG; Donal Sheehan – The 
BRIDE Project – Biodiversity Regeneration 
in a dairying Environment; Sean O’Farrell – 
Farming for Nature – Ambassador Farmer; 
Ailbhe Gerrard – Brookfield Farm – Winner 
of the RDS Sustainable Farming, Sustainable 
Living Awards 2019; and Richard Scally – 
IFA – Farming in a Changing Environment. 
Noel Gavigan, Executive Officer – Irish 
Bioenergy Association who spoke about the 
role of Anaerobic Digesters and BioGas as a 
potential income source in farming. 
 
Comhairle na n’Óg 
The last meeting of the year was held for 
Comhairle na n’Óg on the 4th of December 
2019. The members reflected on a busy year 
some of the high lights being attending the 
Dáil as part of the Dáil na n’Og and also a 
successful AGM held on the 15th of October. 
The Agenda for next year was also discussed 
and the group are looking forward to hard 
work and fun in 2020 with some exciting 
topics to work on.  A meeting was held on 
the 11th of December 2019 for new members 
to join Comhairle na n’Óg. Existing 
members took the time to introduce them to 
what Comhairle na n’Óg is all about and 
discuss the agenda for next year.  
 
Music Generation Offaly/Westmeath  
In total MGOW musicians were involved in 
over 70 performances across 10 days in the 
run up to Christmas Eve 2019.  Some of the 
highlights of the programme included the 
Tullamore intergenerational ukulele group 
performing with the choir of St. Joseph’s NS 
in Tullamore Hospital and local schools were 
again invited by Tullamore Parish to be part 
of their annual Carol Service. 
 
DES Innovation Week 
We were delighted to be invited to perform 
as part of the Department of Education and 
Science’s new initiative, Innovation Week.  
Over the course of a week, employees of the 
DES have the chance to find out more about 
the DES’s work through a range of activities 
and events.  As part of the programme, an 
invitation was issued to Music Generation 
and in turn to MGOW.  We brought a school 
to perform in the DES Tullamore office and 
members of our Mullingar Music Jam were 
bussed down to perform in the DES Athlone 
office.  (See https://bit.ly/2s19zH0  for 
further details.)

Engagement 
with

Exhibition Programme 
The exhibition for October –December was 
‘A Conscious Place for Living’ by Julie 
Spollen. The exhibition uses themes of 
Places, Engagement, Personal & Community 
Narratives to promote access to artistic 
expression that enables societal inclusion. 
The exhibition forms one element of a 
collaboration with visual artist Rowena 
Keaveny into the research of a Creative 
Charter by Older People for Older People; 
Spaces – Identity Participation Equality, in 
partnership with individual Offaly Active 
Age Groups and relevant support networks.  
 
Public Art 
Jessica Traynor who was awarded the 
Banagher Public Art Literature Commission 
hosted a free public creative writing 
workshops in November and continues to 
develop links within the community to 
develop her oral history recording project, 
schools' writing and choral workshops, 
mentorship opportunities for local writers 
and events in conjunction with the That Beats 
Banagher Festival. 
 
Creative Edenderry  
Creative Edenderry faciltated by Voluntary 
Arts Ireland has continued to progress the 
Open Conversations held with individuals 
and local community groups in Edenderry. A 
report and recommendations for next steps 
has been finalized by VAI, for a progression 
plan to be developed early 2020.

national

LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE 
 
Tullamore - Finalist at the Bank of Ireland 
2019 National Enterprise Town Awards 
Tullamore Chamber of Commerce, Offaly 
County Council, and LEO Offaly were well 
represented at the National Final held in 
Kilkenny. While unsuccessful on the night, 
the group had the opportunity to showcase 
many of Tullamore's strengths at the judging 
event that took place in October. 
 
National LEO Network received the "Best 
Local Government Support to Business 
Award" at the 2019 InBusiness Recognition 
Awards 
This award recognises the Local Enterprise 
Office efforts, supports and achievements in 
2019. 
 
China delegation from Luzhou, China 
Orla Martin, Head of Enterprise in LEO 
Offaly presented an overview of economic 
and tourism opportunities in Offaly at the 
event for a delegation from Luzhou, China. 
The delegation from Luzhou, a city with a 
population of over four million, travelled to 
Tullamore Municipal District in order to 
discuss cooperation in the fields of economy, 
trade and tourism.  
A memorandum of understanding was 
signed linking Tullamore with the city of 
Luzhou in China at Tullamore Municipal 
District offices by Mayor Linxing of the city 
of Luzhou and the Cathaoirleach of 
Tullamore Municipal District Councillor 
Frank Moran.

Brexit Customs Workshop - Monday, 24 
February 2020 
The Customs Export & Import Procedures 
workshop will take place in the Tullamore 
Court Hotel on Friday 18th October. It covers 
how export and import customs procedures 
on trade with ‘Third Countries’ apply, how 
tariffs work and the need to correctly classify 
your goods.  
Attendance is free but early booking is 
essential. These workshops are fully funded 
by DBEI, through Enterprise Ireland and are 
delivered by Export-Edge Training, on 
behalf of Local Enterprise Office Offaly.
